title: Cartesian edges give coherent-realization homotopy pullback squares
statement:
Use quasicategories, weak homotopy equivalences and mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and Cartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ from [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration of small quasicategories, let $e:b\to c$ be a $p$-Cartesian edge of $E$, and let $a$ be any vertex of $E$. The strictly commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\mathfrak C[E](a,b)&\xrightarrow{[e]\circ-}&\mathfrak C[E](a,c)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\mathfrak C[B](p(a),p(b))&\xrightarrow{[p(e)]\circ-}&\mathfrak C[B](p(a),p(c))
\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pullback square of simplicial sets. The vertical maps are induced by $\mathfrak C[p]$ and the horizontal maps are enriched composition by the displayed edge morphisms. A homotopy pullback here means that after a functorial Kan replacement of the diagram, the canonical comparison from the upper left corner to the path-space homotopy fiber product of the other three corners is a weak homotopy equivalence. The four unreplaced enriched mapping sets are not assumed Kan.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 (printed pp. 131-132, PDF indices 148-149), via the composition-compatible comparison of Theorem 2.2.5.1; the Cartesian mapping calculation in Proposition 3.2.2.10 (printed p. 184, PDF index 201). Read online 2026-10-17; archival HTT copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-criterion] to the inner fibration p and its p-Cartesian edge e at the vertex a. It gives the homotopy-pullback square of right-pinched mapping spaces with upper horizontal map postcomposition by e, lower horizontal map postcomposition by p(e), and vertical maps induced by p. This is exactly the path-space homotopy-pullback convention used in the item.

Apply [lem-cbc-coherent-square-comparison-data] to $p,e,a$. Its square (i) is the right-pinched square of Step 1, homotopy cartesian there, and its comparison (i)$\to$(ii) supplies corner maps induced by $\alpha_E,\alpha_B$, all weak homotopy equivalences, to the coherent-nerve square (ii). Writing the source square as $(f,g,u,v;H)$, the target as $(f',g',u',v';H')$ and the corner maps as $\bar a,\bar b,\bar c,\bar d$, the node supplies the side homotopies $L,M,N,O$ and the homotopy relative endpoints between the boundary paths $\bar duf\xrightarrow{\bar dH}\bar dvg\xrightarrow{Og}v'\bar cg\xrightarrow{v'M}v'g'\bar a$ and $\bar duf\xrightarrow{Nf}u'\bar bf\xrightarrow{u'L}u'f'\bar a\xrightarrow{H'\bar a}v'g'\bar a$. All corners are mapping spaces of quasicategories, hence Kan. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-kan-homotopy-coherent-cube-invariance] applies, and the coherent-nerve square (ii) is homotopy cartesian.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 and Theorem 2.2.5.1, comparison of the Cartesian mapping square through coherent nerve.

proof.text: Use the comparison (iii)$\to$(ii) of [lem-cbc-coherent-square-comparison-data]. The corners of the enriched square (iii) are Kan because $RD_E,RD_B$ are locally Kan; it commutes strictly because $Rp$ is a simplicial functor and $Rp(r_E[e])=r_B[pe]$ by naturality of $r$, so its commutation homotopy is constant. The node supplies the weak-equivalence corner maps (leg by leg of a zigzag), the side homotopies and the boundary-path homotopy relative endpoints to the coherent-nerve square (ii). Square (ii) is homotopy cartesian by Step 2, so [lem-coef-infinity-kan-homotopy-coherent-cube-invariance], which is stable under zigzags, makes square (iii) homotopy cartesian in its path-space sense with constant homotopy.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 2.4.4.3, locally Kan replacement and coherent transfer.

proof.text: The replacement maps $r_E:D_E\to RD_E$ and $r_B:D_B\to RD_B$ are simplicial functors with $Rp\,r_E=r_B\,\mathfrak C[p]$, so they commute strictly with both vertical maps and both enriched postcomposition maps. They are weak homotopy equivalences on all four mapping simplicial sets by the locally Kan replacement clause of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. For the Kan square (iii), [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition] identifies the two-leg fibration-replacement notion with the path-space comparison after functorial Kan replacement; the replacement maps of the Kan corners are weak equivalences commuting strictly with the square, so by [lem-coef-infinity-kan-homotopy-coherent-cube-invariance] (all side homotopies constant) the path-space condition of Step 3 is the one for the replaced square, and square (iii) is homotopy cartesian in the two-leg sense. Then [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-cartesian-invariance] transfers homotopy cartesianness to the unreplaced enriched square of the item, and [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition] again identifies this with the item's functorial Kan-replacement/path-space definition. Its corners, vertical maps and horizontal maps are exactly those displayed in the item.

lean.statement: theorem coherent_cartesian_postcomposition {E B : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory E] [Quasicategory B] (p : E ⟶ B) (hp : InnerFibration p) (x : E _⦋0⦌) (b c : E _⦋0⦌) (e : Δ[1] ⟶ E) (he₀ : E.δ 1 (SSet.yonedaEquiv e) = b) (he₁ : E.δ 0 (SSet.yonedaEquiv e) = c) (he : Enhanced.IsCartesianEdge p e) : IsFunctorialKanHomotopyPullbackSquare (enrichedPostcomposition (rigidification.obj E) (vertex E x) (vertex E b) (vertex E c) (coherentEdge b c (SSet.yonedaEquiv e) he₀ he₁)) (mappingMap p x b) (mappingMap p x c) (enrichedPostcomposition (rigidification.obj B) (vertex B (p.app _ x)) (vertex B (p.app _ b)) (vertex B (p.app _ c)) (coherentEdge (p.app _ b) (p.app _ c) (p.app _ (SSet.yonedaEquiv e)) (by simpa only [SimplicialObject.δ] using (p.naturality_apply (SimplexCategory.δ 1).op (SSet.yonedaEquiv e)).symm.trans (congrArg (p.app _) he₀)) (by simpa only [SimplicialObject.δ] using (p.naturality_apply (SimplexCategory.δ 0).op (SSet.yonedaEquiv e)).symm.trans (congrArg (p.app _) he₁))))
